<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: dispatch-resume-command-assembly -->
### Problem

`local/bin/dispatch.sh --resume <thread>` currently invokes the installed CLI with
global `codex exec` options after the `resume` subcommand. The CLI rejects `-C` in that
position, so sanctioned resume attempts fail before a thread starts. The 2026-09-03
issue #18 attempt was recorded as failed session `orc-18-20260903-01`; earlier workflow
sessions show the same failure shape.

### Scope

- Assemble global `codex exec` options before the optional `resume` subcommand.
- Preserve resume-specific model, configuration, JSON capture, sandbox, and final-message
  behavior without bypassing `dispatch.sh` telemetry.
- Add deterministic command-assembly or CLI smoke coverage for both fresh and resumed
  sessions.
- Update `local/protocols/sessions.md` only if the documented invocation changes.

### Acceptance criteria

- A fresh dispatched session and a resumed thread both start in the requested worktree.
- Both paths emit JSON events, a thread id, a final-message capture, and one correct
  `sessions.jsonl` record.
- Existing hook checks, worktree locking, trusted-persona loading, and prompt-size guards
  remain intact.
- Local workflow tests and an end-to-end resume smoke test pass.

This tooling repair does not block the mathematics queue; issue #18 continues in a fresh
sanctioned session.

title: Progress log - stage reports from the operator session (pinned)

labels.name: tracking
labels.description: Umbrella issue whose children are tracked via parent/children frontmatter

body:
<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: progress-log-stage-reports-from-the-operator-session-b93ce91f -->
Pinned, always open. The operator session (qpbt-main) appends one comment here at every stage boundary and whenever a PR merges, so the owner can follow progress from GitHub without attaching to the tmux session.

## Format (one comment per report)

​`​`​`
### <date> — <stage> — <headline>
**Merged:** PR numbers and heads (or "none").
**Dispatched:** issues/worktrees in flight and their state.
**Next:** the next queue item.
**Blocked:** "none", or the BLOCKER ids open in the Owner inbox.
​`​`​`

Keep each report under ~20 lines; link PRs and issues by number. Decisions needed from the owner never go here — they go to the pinned "Owner inbox" issue.

title: Owner inbox - decisions needed from the owner (pinned; one BLOCKER per comment)

labels.name: needs-owner
labels.description: Blocked on an owner decision; the operator has parked this item and continues with the queue

body:
This issue is the single place where the operator session (qpbt-main) asks the owner for a decision. It stays open and pinned; nothing else uses the `needs-owner` label. The owner is a human who checks GitHub occasionally and wants to catch up in one minute; every comment here also reaches the owner by email.

## When to post here — the test

Post ONLY if all three hold:
1. the item cannot move at all without the owner (credentials; the scope budget `MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE`; a mathematical design choice that changes what is being proved or what the paper claims);
2. no protocol, persona rule, or standing briefing lets you decide it yourself — if one does, decide, record the reason in `results/telemetry/events.md`, and continue;
3. you have already parked the item and have other queue work to do meanwhile.

If in doubt, decide it yourself and record it. A wrong self-decision is recoverable; an idle project is not. Reviewer findings, workflow ergonomics, tooling choices, and "which order" questions are never owner blockers.

## Format — plain and short (hard cap: 10 lines above the fold)

Write for a human who has not seen the project in days. No jargon, no SHAs, no file paths above the fold, no protocol section numbers. Question first.

```
### BLOCKER <id> — <plain title, ≤ 8 words>
<!-- owner-inbox id=<id> status=open -->
**What I need from you:** one question, with the options (A/B/…) and which one I recommend and why, in ≤ 3 sentences.
**Why only you can decide:** one sentence.
**What happens meanwhile:** one sentence (what I am working on instead; nothing is waiting idle).
<details><summary>Details, if you want them</summary>
Issue/PR numbers, heads, file paths, the full reasoning, alternatives considered.
</details>
```

`<id>` is `B` + a running number (B1, B2, …). One blocker per comment. Do not repeat a blocker; do not add commentary.

**Owner — to answer:** reply with a comment starting with `DECISION <id>:` in plain words (e.g. `DECISION B3: agree`, or `DECISION B3: option B, and also …`).

**Operator — closing the loop:** at the start of every loop iteration and at every stage boundary, read this issue's comments (`gh api repos/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/26/comments --paginate`), find `DECISION <id>` comments for ids still `status=open`, act, then post `RESOLVED <id>: <one line>` and edit the original BLOCKER comment's marker to `status=resolved`. A blocker with no decision stays parked; never re-ask.

**Everything else** (progress, stage reports, what merged / what is dispatched / what is next) goes to the pinned "Progress log" issue #27, not here.

Follow-up from the 2026-09-02 owner-stall audit (see EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-02 and issue #20 / PR #21). PR #21 fixed the sites on the PR #5 stall path; the rest are wording only and deliberately out of that episode's scope.

title: Lean skeleton: QPBT file tree and the statement of thm:pauli
body:
### Precise mathematical statement

Stage 4.1 (sub-issue of #0001): a minimal Lean skeleton under
`MIPStarRE/QPBT/` carrying the faithful statement of `thm:pauli`
(soundness/self-testing of the Pauli basis test, soundness function
$\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b+q^{-b}+2^{-bmd})$)
and every definition its statement transitively uses, with all proofs
`sorry`.

### Mathematical source

- Paper: `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`,
  label `thm:pauli`.
- Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, label `thm:pauli`,
  statement closure through `ch12_qpbt_games.tex` and `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex`.

### Target Lean declaration

`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` (statement only, proof `sorry`) plus the
transitive definition closure; design brief at
`issues/briefs/0006-minimal-skeleton-brief.md`.

### Mathematical dependencies

- Reusable infrastructure: `MIPStarRE.Quantum` (matrices, measurements),
  selected `MIPStarRE.LDT` declarations per the brief's REUSE column.
- Encoding decisions: polynomial representatives (issue #0004 note);
  distribution encoding matched to the LDT track's.

### Proof plan

Explain the mathematical argument to be formalized, including any deliberate
deviation from the paper or blueprint statement.

### Statement integrity

Paper assumptions, Lean assumptions, paper conclusion, Lean conclusion, and a
verdict: exact / faithful boundary hypotheses / extra assumptions / weakened
